title: language-agnostic contract adapter: schema-guided invocation + fuzzing/backoff helpers
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Problem: Current SDK helpers for function/tool calling lack a unified, language-agnostic approach for runtime schema validation, robust retries, and streaming resume semantics. Different languages use divergent validator libraries and retry heuristics, which leads to inconsistent developer ergonomics and production surprises (silent schema coercions, unhelpful error messages, or duplicate side effects during retries).

Goal: Implement a cross-SDK "Contract Adapter" that provides: a) pluggable schema validation (sync/async), b) deterministic coercion and clear errors, c) idempotent invocation wrappers for safe retries, d) streaming iterators that support resumable consumption via compact resume tokens, and e) optional fuzzing harness for CI to detect schema/regression mismatches. The solution must be ergonomic for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs and align with the Redwood API semantics (function metadata, arguments, streaming chunks).

Design notes:
- Validation strategy: Accept model-provided JSON Schema + SDK-supplied contract hints. Provide a thin-shim that selects best-in-class runtime validator per language (ajv in TS, jsonschema/fastjsonschema in Python, gojsonschema in Go). Expose a uniform error envelope with: code, path, suggested fix, and example value.
- Coercion: Offer opt-in coercion rules (numbers-as-strings, null->empty, enum-canonicalization) with a deterministic precedence list and per-field opt-out via schema annotations.
- Invocation wrapper: provide a RetryCoordinator that supports: idempotency_key injection, once-only side-effect guards for functions marked side_effect: true, exponential/backoff jitter policy, and transparent fallback to a safe non-retry path when function response indicates non-idempotent side effects.
- Streaming ergonomics: streaming helpers expose an async iterator (Py/TS) or channel (+ iterator) (Go), and persist a compact resume token (sequence index + KV cache fingerprint). Resume token size must be <= 512 bytes and verifiable by the runtime. The adapter will coordinate KV cache warming and request replay limits to avoid duplicate side effects.
- Fuzzing & tests: include a lightweight CI job that fuzzes argument shapes against known schemas to detect regressions in coercion/validation logic and to exercise retry semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Unified validator API exists in Python/TS/Go with same error envelope and documented opt-in coercion rules
Invocation wrapper automatically injects idempotency_key and prevents automatic retries for marked side-effectful functions
Streaming iterator supports resume tokens and includes a demo showing resume across a simulated dropped connection
Fuzzing CI detects at least 3 schema/coercion regressions on a seeded mutation corpus
End-to-end SDK examples added to docs and quickstarts for all three languages
Benchmark: validation + invocation helper adds <5ms median overhead for small payloads on hosted SDK benchmark
work_breakdown: spec: contract adapter API + error envelope (author: Priya)
TS: explorer module using ajv + retry coordinator + streaming iterator wrapper (owner: Aisha)
Python: thin adapter using jsonschema/fastjsonschema + async iterator and resume token logic (owner: Jonas Müller)
Go: sync iterator + channel wrapper, gojsonschema integration, and resume token helper (owner: Caleb Wong)
CI: fuzzing harness and mutation corpus + flaky-run gating (owner: QA)
Docs: examples for Python/TS/Go + migration guide for existing SDK users (owner: DevRel)
E2E tests: simulated network drop, non-idempotent function abort, schema mismatch regression suite
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Validator performance and cold-start overhead could impact latency. Mitigation: allow precompiled validators and lazy initialization; benchmark and add warmup path in Dedicated environments.

Risk: Resume tokens could enable replay of side effects. Mitigation: require server-side token verification + client-side limited replay attempts and explicit opt-in for resume on side-effectful functions.
Risk: Divergent language behaviors lead to subtle user surprises. Mitigation: shared conformance tests and CI fuzzing across all SDKs; surface semantic diffs in the docs.
Risk: Schema coercion may mask upstream bugs. Mitigation: coercion is opt-in and logged; CI will run with coercion disabled by default to detect violations.
Risk: Security review required for idempotency and token formats. Mitigation: request security review early and document threat model.
Risk: Large schemas increase memory. Mitigation: cache compiled validators and support streaming validation for very large payloads.
rollout_plan: MVP: library-level implementation + Python + TS examples behind feature flag; internal dogfooding with Redwood Console routes
Beta: enable Go, add CI fuzzing job, expand docs and publish migration guide
GA: default enablement in SDKs, release notes with migration steps and opt-out instructions
